Questions:
Main Question:
How accurately can we predict the accuracy of a poll based on the sampled population?
(We'd want to fit a binomial to find accuracy of actual predictions win/loss. Additionally,
do lm to find actual percentages. Can compare absolute accuracy of binary outcome versus 
percentage accuracy, both are important. Do this for both 2012 and 2016 data.)

Sub Questions:
How do different methods and factors in a polled population affect the accuracy of polls?
(This is analysis of different models, ANOVA, possibly trying forward/backward/both stepwise,
do the stuff from this week to check for overfitting)

How much do unexpected results affect the accuracy of prediction?
(Out of the incorrect predictions, were these outliers/unexpected results? (Landslide win
when predicting 50/50ish). Check this by looking at residual vs fitted plots/similar.
Look at cooks distance for polls as well? After making a model, check if removing these
improves prediction. DO NOT PHRASE THIS AS IMPROVING THE MODEL. THIS IS NOT IMPROVING THE MODEL.
WE WOULD DO THIS TO SEE HOW MUCH OUTLIERS AFFECTED OUR MODELS AFTER THE FACT. This can 
help future models, outliers being significant here means outliers may be significant in
other polls.)

## Data
- Patrick dibs

Describe the data accurately: its source, the unit of observation, the variables
used, and any cleaning or exclusions. The example uses the built-in `mtcars`
data [@rcore], covering `r n_obs` vehicles. Summarise the key variables as in
@tbl-descriptives.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptives
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the variables used in the analysis."
data |>
  summarise(
    across(c(mpg, wt, hp),
           list(mean = mean, sd = sd),
           .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = c("Variable", ".value"),

  kable(digits = 2, col.names = c("Variable", "Mean", "SD"))
```

# Results {#sec-results}

<!-- See rubric: Results - describe analysis w.r.t. the question; visualise; check assumptions. -->

@fig-relationship shows the relationship between weight and fuel economy, with a
fitted regression line. The estimated model is reported in @tbl-model: each
additional 1000 lbs is associated with a change of `r round(wt_beta, 1)` mpg,
and the model explains `r round(100 * r2, 1)`% of the variation in fuel economy.
Model assumptions are checked in @sec-appendix.

```{r}
#| label: fig-relationship
#| fig-cap: "Fuel economy against vehicle weight, with a fitted linear regression line and 95% confidence band."
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3.2
ggplot(data, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
  labs(x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "Fuel economy (mpg)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model
#| tbl-cap: "Linear regression of fuel economy (mpg) on weight and horsepower."
# modelsummary's default `tinytable` backend renders cleanly to PDF.
modelsummary(
  list("Fuel economy (mpg)" = model),
  coef_map = c("wt" = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
               "hp" = "Horsepower",
               "(Intercept)" = "Intercept"),
  gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared", "adj.r.squared"),
  stars = TRUE
)
```

# Statistical appendix {#sec-appendix}

<!-- See rubric: Statistical appendix - fully reproducible, annotated analysis. -->

This appendix documents the analysis so the results above are fully reproducible.
The annotated code reproduces the model and its assumption checks; the complete
project (data, scripts, and commit history) is in the repository linked at the
top.

## Model {#sec-app-model}

@tbl-model-detail reports the full fitted model with 95% confidence intervals.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-detail
#| tbl-cap: "Full regression results, with 95% confidence intervals."
#| echo: true
# Fit the model and report it as a formatted table (not raw console output)
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)

modelsummary(
  list("Fuel economy (mpg)" = model),
  statistic = "conf.int",                       # 95% CIs beneath each estimate
  coef_map  = c("wt" = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
                "hp" = "Horsepower",
                "(Intercept)" = "Intercept"),
  gof_map   = c("nobs", "r.squared", "adj.r.squared")
)
```

## Assumption checks {#sec-app-checks}

@fig-diagnostics shows the residual diagnostics used to check the linear-model
assumptions of constant variance and approximately normal residuals.

```{r}
#| label: fig-diagnostics
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Residual diagnostics: residuals vs fitted values (left) and a normal Q-Q plot (right)."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.2
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(model, which = 1)   # residuals vs fitted: linearity and equal variance
plot(model, which = 2)   # normal Q-Q: normality of residuals
```
